method.label: A linear quotient and matching coefficients

annotationRationale: The common distinct roots establish divisibility. Expanding the linear quotient times the cubic and matching coefficients determines the parameters needed for evaluation.
sourceMethod: Followed the official factorization f(x)=(x-q)g(x), coefficient comparison, and evaluation at 1. Added the justification that three distinct shared roots make g a factor of f.

review.mathCheck: The three distinct shared roots imply g divides f. The monic linear quotient gives 10-q=100 and a-q=1, hence q=-90 and a=-89. Therefore f(1)=91(-77)=-7007, choice C. No additional parameter values are needed for this evaluation.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, independently worded adaptation of MAA solution 23 on page 10: introduce the additional linear factor, compare the x and x-cubed coefficients, then evaluate the product at 1.
review.annotationCheck: Factor/divisibility reasoning and coefficient comparison are correctly assessed. Polynomial multiplication is appropriate support. The distinct-root condition is explicitly used.
